answer: A datacenter or proxy pool as a result cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch whatever the capital it holds, because each identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. The haven cap is enforced at intake and opal shows the per-origin counts. At most 1 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a vertex tag. That is 10 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
